references.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Zeno’s Paradoxes
references.support: Scholarly discussion of Aristotle’s later report, modern reconstructions of the Dichotomy, mathematical replies, and qualifications concerning infinity and the physical application of the continuum. Relevant sections were read; the full entry was not.

references.title: Aristotle, Physics, Book VI
references.support: Primary ancient text in the Hardie and Gaye translation: Book VI.9 reports the half-way argument and presents Aristotle’s response about infinitely divisible magnitude and time. Selected passages were read; the complete Physics was not.

references.title: Aristotle, Physics, Book III
references.support: Primary ancient text in the Hardie and Gaye translation: Book III.6 discusses the infinite by division and potential existence. The relevant passage was read; the complete Physics was not.

references.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Supertasks
references.support: Scholarly reference discussion of the forward and regressive Zeno walk, geometric-series convergence and meanings of completion, and Thomson’s lamp as a related but distinct discrete supertask. Relevant sections were read; the full entry was not.
